s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Article 15(4) into the Constitution of India following the Champakam Dorairajan case?
x: The First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951 inserted Article 15(4), enabling special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and SCs and STs.
tq: Directly identify the amendment associated with a specific constitutional article.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: Article 16(4A), relating to reservation in promotion for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, was inserted by the
x: The 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995 inserted Article 16(4A) to provide reservation in promotion for SCs and STs, in response to the Indra Sawhney judgment.
tq: Use the article-number and amendment-number association to distinguish closely related reservation amendments.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: The 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001 provided for
o: identification of SEBCs by the States
consequential seniority in promotion and nullified the catch-up rule
reservation in private unaided educational institutions including minority institutions
x: The 85th Amendment provided consequential seniority along with promotion and nullified the catch-up rule.
tq: Use a distinctive legal consequence to identify the correct amendment.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s:
With reference to the 93rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2005, consider the following statements:
1. It inserted Article 15(5).
2. It enabled reservation in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions.
3. Minority educational institutions were excluded from its scope.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5) and enabled reservation in educational institutions, including private unaided institutions, while excluding minority institutions.
tq: Test the main provision together with its important constitutional exception.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 103rd Amendment — Constitutional status to the NCBC
x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 gave constitutional status to the NCBC through Article 338B and inserted Article 342A. Article 15(5) belongs to the 93rd Amendment, EWS reservation to the 103rd, and restoration of States' power to the 105th.
tq: Trap article and amendment swaps by matching each amendment with its exact constitutional change.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 is associated with
o: 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central educational institutions
restoration of States' power to identify SEBCs
10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections and amendments to Articles 15 and 16
reservation in promotion for SCs and STs
x: The 103rd Amendment introduced 10 per cent reservation for EWS and amended Articles 15 and 16 for this purpose.
tq: Identify the famous policy measure associated with the amendment rather than a neighbouring reservation provision.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: Which of the following correctly represents the amendment and the corresponding Constitutional Amendment Bill?
x: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act was enacted from the 124th Constitutional Amendment Bill. The 102nd and 105th Amendments corresponded to the 123rd and 127th Bills respectively.
tq: Distinguish the enacted amendment number from the preceding bill number.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The 82nd Amendment concerns relaxation of qualifying standards in promotion for SCs and STs.
The 81st Amendment deals with unfilled backlog vacancies.
The 89th Amendment introduced the relaxation of qualifying marks under Article 335.
The 77th Amendment deals with reservation in promotion for SCs and STs.
x: The 89th Amendment did not introduce the relaxation of qualifying marks; that change was made by the 82nd Amendment Act, 2000. The 89th Amendment is associated with the bifurcation of the SC/ST Commission.
tq: Find the wrong amendment-provision association among closely related reservation amendments.
sec: Constitutional amendments on reservation → content and bill numbers

s: Under Article 340 of the Constitution, a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes is appointed by the
o: Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment
x: Article 340 empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes and recommend remedial measures.
tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the constitutional authority.

s: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission did not accept which of the following as the criterion for identifying backward classes?
o: Poor representation in trade and industry
x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission did not accept caste as the criterion, although its broader criteria included educational and occupational disadvantage and inadequate representation.
tq: Test the crucial distinction between the criteria considered and the criterion rejected.

s: The Second Backward Classes Commission, popularly known as the Mandal Commission, was set up in 1979 by the
x: The B.P. Mandal Commission was established in 1979 by the Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai.
tq: Avoid the common trap of confusing the government that appointed a commission with the government that implemented its recommendations.

s: The Mandal Commission recommended reservation of what percentage of posts for Other Backward Classes?
x: The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs. Its estimate that OBCs constituted 52 per cent of the population was a population figure, not the recommended quota.
tq: Distinguish the recommended reservation percentage from the estimated share of the population.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations?
o: They were implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1990, and 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved in 1993.
They were implemented by the V.P. Singh Government in 1993, and posts were reserved in 1995.
They were implemented by the Morarji Desai Government in 1979, and posts were reserved in 1980.
They were implemented by the Nehru Government in 1955, and posts were reserved in 1990.
x: The V.P. Singh Government implemented the Mandal recommendations in 1990, and 27 per cent of Central civil posts were reserved for OBCs in 1993.
tq: Track the sequence of appointment, report, political implementation and operational reservation.

s: The Mandal Commission used how many indicators covering social, educational and economic factors?
x: The Mandal Commission used 11 indicators covering social, educational and economic dimensions of backwardness.
tq: Recall the exact quantitative detail attached to the commission's methodology.

s: Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 primarily for
o: identifying the first list of OBCs under Article 340
determining the constitutional validity of EWS reservation
preparing the list of Scheduled Tribes
x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in 2017 to examine the sub-categorisation of OBCs.
tq: Match the commission's name and year with its specific mandate.

s: Which of the following observations is associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 3 per cent of benefits went to 97 per cent of the sub-castes.
All OBC communities received an equal share of reservation benefits.
Nearly 52 per cent of the population received 27 per cent reservation.
Around 97 per cent of OBC benefits went to 25 per cent of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities received none.
x: The Rohini Commission's findings indicated that approximately 97 per cent of OBC benefits went to 25 per cent of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities received no benefits.
tq: Handle paired percentages and community counts without reversing their relationship.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the two early Backward Classes Commissions is correct?
o: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission listed about 2,399 castes, whereas the Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population.
The Kaka Kalelkar Commission was appointed in 1979 and the Mandal Commission in 1953.
Both commissions were appointed by the V.P. Singh Government.
Both commissions recommended 27 per cent reservation and were fully implemented.
x: The Kaka Kalelkar Commission's report listed about 2,399 castes, while the Mandal Commission estimated OBCs at 52 per cent of the population. The two commissions differed in date, government and outcome.
tq: Compare corresponding rows of the two commission profiles rather than memorising isolated names.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution expressly defines the term 'backward classes'.
2. Article 340 enables the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of SEBCs.
3. The Mandal Commission was appointed under Article 340.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Constitution does not define the expression 'backward classes'; Article 340 provides for a commission to investigate their conditions and recommend remedies.
tq: Use the negative constitutional fact to eliminate the statement that sounds formally plausible but is incorrect.

s: Before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment, Article 338(10) provided that references to Scheduled Castes would include such backward classes as were specified by the
x: Before the 102nd Amendment, Article 338(10) treated references to Scheduled Castes as including such backward classes as the President specified. Consequently, complaints relating to backward classes could go to the SC Commission.
tq: Identify the constitutional authority named in the transitional provision.

s: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment added Article 366(26C), which defines Socially and Educationally Backward Classes by reference to
x: Article 366(26C), added by the 102nd Amendment, defines SEBCs by reference to Article 342A.
tq: Distinguish the defining provision from the related provisions on reservation, commissions and promotion.

s: The Supreme Court judgment in which case struck down the Madras Communal Government Order and led to the First Constitutional Amendment?
o: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore
Champakam Dorairajan v. State of Madras
Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India
x: In Champakam Dorairajan (1951), the Madras Communal Government Order was struck down, leading to the First Constitutional Amendment.
tq: Identify the case from the specific constitutional consequence.

s:
With reference to M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore, consider the following statements:
1. Caste cannot be the sole test for determining backwardness.
2. Reservation should generally remain below 50 per cent.
3. The case upheld reservation without prescribing any requirement of reasonableness.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The judgment emphasised that reservation must be reasonable and that caste cannot be the sole test; statement 3 is incorrect.
tq: Find the false statement by testing the omitted qualification of reasonableness.

s: In Indra Sawhney v. Union of India, the constitutional validity of the 27 per cent reservation for OBCs was upheld by a nine-judge Bench by what majority?
x: The nine-judge Bench decided Indra Sawhney by a 6:3 majority and upheld the 27 per cent OBC quota subject to exclusion of the creamy layer.
tq: Use the distinctive bench-strength and majority figures together.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a holding of the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney (1992)?
o: A general ceiling of 50 per cent on reservations
Reservation in promotions for backward classes as a general rule
Exclusion of the creamy layer from OBC reservation
Establishment of a permanent body for backward classes
x: Indra Sawhney did not permit reservation in promotions as a general rule. It upheld 27 per cent OBC reservation, excluded the creamy layer, prescribed a 50 per cent ceiling subject to exceptional cases, and directed creation of a permanent backward-classes body.
tq: Eliminate the option that reverses the case’s principal limitation.

s:
The judgment in M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006) upheld the constitutional amendments relating to reservation in promotion subject to which conditions?
1. Backwardness must be established.
2. Inadequate representation must be supported by quantifiable data.
3. Administrative efficiency must be considered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three conditions were recognised in M. Nagaraj: backwardness, inadequate representation supported by quantifiable data, and preservation of administrative efficiency.
tq: Treat a complete list of conditions as correct only when every condition belongs to the judgment.

s: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India is associated with upholding which of the following amendments, subject to conditions?
x: M. Nagaraj (2006) upheld the 77th and 85th Constitutional Amendments concerning reservation in promotion, subject to specified constitutional conditions.
tq: Match the case with the precise amendment pair.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008):
1. It upheld the 93rd Constitutional Amendment.
2. It upheld the 2006 law concerning reservation in State and aided institutions.
3. It held that the creamy layer among OBCs need not be excluded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The creamy layer had to be excluded, so statement 3 is incorrect.
tq: Spot the reversed position on creamy-layer exclusion.

s:
With reference to Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (November 2022), consider the following statements:
1. The EWS reservation was upheld by a 3:2 majority.
2. The 50 per cent ceiling was held to apply to backward-class reservations, but not to EWS reservation.
3. The judgment was delivered unanimously.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The EWS reservation was upheld in Janhit Abhiyan by a 3:2 majority. The 50 per cent ceiling was treated as applicable to backward-class reservations and not to EWS; statement 3 is false because the Bench was divided.
tq: Use the majority figure to reject the absolute word in the third statement.

s: The Supreme Court’s decision in Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. State of Maharashtra (2021) primarily concerned which issue?
o: Validity of the Maratha reservation exceeding the 50 per cent ceiling
Validity of reservation for SC converts to Christianity
Exclusion of the creamy layer from EWS reservation
x: The Maratha quota was struck down for crossing the 50 per cent ceiling without exceptional circumstances.
tq: Identify the case from its distinctive reservation group and ceiling issue.

s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the 105th Constitutional Amendment (2021) in relation to the Maratha reservation judgment?
o: It removed the 50 per cent ceiling in all reservation matters.
It abolished the Central list of SEBCs.
It reversed the reading of the 102nd Amendment that had restricted the States’ power to identify SEBCs.
It prohibited States from maintaining backward-class lists.
x: The 105th Amendment reversed the interpretation of the 102nd Amendment in the Maratha case and restored the States’ power to identify socially and educationally backward classes.
tq: Test the constitutional amendment as a corrective response to a judicial interpretation.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Case)
A. Champakam Dorairajan
B. M.R. Balaji
C. M. Nagaraj
D. Jarnail Singh

List-II (Principal issue)
1. Conditions for reservation in promotion
2. Madras Communal Government Order
3. Caste not being the sole test and reservation below 50 per cent
4. Creamy layer in SC/ST promotions

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Champakam Dorairajan concerned the Communal Government Order; M.R. Balaji concerned caste and the 50 per cent principle; M. Nagaraj concerned promotional reservation conditions; Jarnail Singh concerned creamy layer in SC/ST promotions.
tq: Start from the sure case-issue pairs and eliminate incompatible codes.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, which group is associated with aboriginal tribes, Vimukta Jatis and nomadic groups?
x: BC-A comprises aboriginal tribes, Vimukta Jatis and nomadic groups and has a 7 per cent quota.
tq: Discriminate between closely related BC group labels and their social composition.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to the Andhra Pradesh BC groups?
o: BC-E — aboriginal tribes and nomadic groups
x: BC-D consists of other classes. BC-B comprises vocational or occupational groups, BC-C comprises SC converts to Christianity, and BC-E comprises socially and educationally backward Muslims.
tq: Use the group-composition pairs to detect swapped categories.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following pairs relating to BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. BC-A — 7 per cent
2. BC-B — 10 per cent
3. BC-C — 1 per cent
4. BC-D — 7 per cent
5. BC-E — 4 per cent
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All five pairs are correct. The respective shares are BC-A 7 per cent, BC-B 10 per cent, BC-C 1 per cent, BC-D 7 per cent and BC-E 4 per cent.
tq: Check every numerical pair individually before selecting the complete combination.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: The BC-E category in Andhra Pradesh was added through which measure and in which year?
x: BC-E was added by the Andhra Pradesh Act of 2007. Earlier lists commonly included only BC-A to BC-D.
tq: Match the category’s introduction with the specific legal instrument and year.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the Andhra Pradesh Muslim quota in chronological order:
A. The 2004 quota was struck down.
B. The 2005 quota was struck down.
C. The 2007 Act providing a 4 per cent quota was enacted.
D. The 2007 Act was struck down by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in 2010.
x: The 2004 and 2005 quotas were struck down first, followed by the 2007 Act providing 4 per cent reservation, which was struck down by the High Court in 2010.
tq: Fix the years first and then arrange the two earlier quota decisions.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: What was the effect of the Supreme Court’s interim order concerning the 4 per cent reservation for backward Muslim groups in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It permanently approved the quota without further judicial examination.
It allowed the quota to continue pending consideration by a Constitution Bench.
It converted the quota into an EWS reservation.
It abolished the quota immediately after the High Court judgment.
x: Although the Andhra Pradesh High Court struck down the 2007 Act in 2010, the Supreme Court permitted the 4 per cent quota to continue by an interim order pending a Constitution Bench.
tq: Distinguish an interim continuation from final constitutional approval.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Kapu reservation proposal is correct?
1. The Justice Manjunatha Commission was constituted in 2016.
2. A 2017 Bill proposed 5 per cent reservation for Kapus as BC-F.
3. The proposal was approved by the Centre.
4. In 2019, Kapus received 5 per cent reservation within the 10 per cent EWS quota, which was later withdrawn by the succeeding government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Centre never approved the 2017 BC-F proposal, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Find the wrong authority-action statement among otherwise connected facts.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: The combined quota shares of BC-A, BC-B, BC-C, BC-D and BC-E in Andhra Pradesh amount to:
x: The shares are 7 per cent, 10 per cent, 1 per cent, 7 per cent and 4 per cent respectively, totalling 29 per cent.
tq: Add the category-wise figures rather than confusing them with the local-body quota.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: After 1956, which arrangement was made in relation to backward-class lists in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Separate lists were prepared only for Rayalaseema and Coastal Andhra.
Separate BC lists were maintained for Andhra and Telangana, containing 86 castes for Andhra.
A single list was prepared for the entire State without regional distinction.
BC lists were abolished and replaced by the EWS list.
x: After 1956, separate backward-class lists existed for Andhra and Telangana; the Andhra list contained 86 castes.
tq: Test the regional administrative distinction and the associated number together.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: What was provided by the 1963 Government Order relating to backward classes in Andhra Pradesh?
o: 5 per cent reservation for Kapus as BC-F
4 per cent reservation for backward Muslims
20 per cent of local-body seats for BCs
25 per cent of medical seats for 139 castes
x: The 1963 Government Order provided 25 per cent of medical seats for 139 castes.
tq: Match the Government Order with its sector, percentage and caste count.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: The Sukhdev case concerning backward-class reservation in Andhra Pradesh resulted in which of the following conclusions?
o: Caste alone could not be the basis, and 112 classes were identified using poverty, residence and occupation.
All reservation for backward classes was unconstitutional.
Caste alone could be the basis for identifying backward classes.
Reservation could be based only on residence.
x: The High Court held in the Sukhdev case that caste alone could not be the basis; consequently, 112 classes were listed using poverty, residence and occupation as considerations.
tq: Link the judicial principle with the resulting classification exercise.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: Which commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission and framed the A-D grouping along with a 25 per cent quota?
x: The Anantharaman Commission was the first Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission; its report was submitted in 1970 and it framed the A-D grouping and a 25 per cent quota.
tq: Identify the commission from its distinctive first-commission and grouping role.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Muralidhara Rao Commission?
o: It was constituted in 2016 to examine Kapu reservation only.
It decided the constitutional validity of EWS reservation in 2022.
It took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation and examined inclusion of minorities.
x: The Muralidhara Rao Commission took charge on 27 January 1982, reviewed BC reservation, examined minority inclusion and contributed to a higher total quota.
tq: Use the commission’s date and subject of inquiry to distinguish it from other bodies.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding reservation for BCs in Andhra Pradesh local bodies:
1. NTR introduced a 20 per cent BC quota in 1984.
2. The quota was raised to 34 per cent for polls held in 1995, 2001, 2006 and 2013.
3. It was subsequently reduced to 24.15 per cent under Government Orders 176, 559 and 560.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: the quota began at 20 per cent in 1984, rose to 34 per cent for the specified elections, and was later reduced to 24.15 per cent under the cited Government Orders.
tq: Track the changing percentage chronologically and retain the order-specific details.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: According to the stated current arrangement for Andhra Pradesh local bodies, the BC quota is:
o: 34 per cent in rural and 33.33 per cent in urban local bodies
29 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
33.33 per cent in rural and 34 per cent in urban local bodies
24.15 per cent in rural and 20 per cent in urban local bodies
x: The stated arrangement provides 34 per cent reservation in rural local bodies and 33.33 per cent in urban local bodies.
tq: Compare the rural and urban figures without reversing their order.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 relates to BC reservation in urban local-body elections under which laws?
o: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965
The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1965 and the Panchayat Raj Act, 1994
x: G.O. Rt. No. 1065 dated 19 August 2026 concerns urban local-body polls under the AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 and the Municipalities Act, 1965.
tq: Match the Government Order with the correct pair of statutes and date.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s:
The Supreme Court’s triple test for OBC reservation in local bodies requires:
1. A dedicated commission to examine backwardness.
2. Determination of the reservation proportion local-body-wise.
3. Keeping the total reservation within the 50 per cent ceiling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three requirements form the triple test: a dedicated commission, local-body-wise proportional determination, and compliance with the overall 50 per cent ceiling.
tq: Recognise a judicial test as a cumulative set of mandatory conditions.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: The earlier 34 per cent reservation for BCs in Andhra Pradesh local bodies was struck down primarily because it:
o: Was introduced through a Constitutional Amendment
Was confined to urban local bodies only
x: The earlier 34 per cent local-body reservation was struck down for breaching the overall reservation ceiling.
tq: Identify the constitutional limitation triggered by the percentage claimed.
sec: OBC reservation in AP - BC groups, Muslim quota, Kapus  [APPSC]

s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to provide reservation for Economically Weaker Sections?
x: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment, enacted in January 2019, inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for EWS reservation.
tq: Use the amendment-number and provision pairing to distinguish closely related constitutional amendments.

s:
With reference to reservation for Economically Weaker Sections, consider the following statements:
1. It may extend up to 10 per cent.
2. It is available only to persons covered by SC, ST or OBC quotas.
3. It is in addition to the existing reservation quotas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: EWS reservation may extend up to 10 per cent and is additional to existing quotas. It is meant for persons not covered by SC, ST or OBC reservation.
tq: Split the options by checking the exclusion condition in statement 2.

s:
The constitutional provisions relating to EWS reservation are applicable to which of the following institutions or sectors?
1. Central educational institutions
2. Private educational institutions
3. Posts under the Central Government
4. State Governments on a compulsory basis
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The 103rd Amendment provides EWS reservation in central educational institutions, including private institutions, and in posts. Its implementation is not mandatory for State Governments.
tq: Identify the statement that overstates the constitutional obligation by using a compulsory application to States.

s: For determining EWS eligibility, which one of the following combinations correctly represents the income and asset criteria stated for the purpose?
o: Annual family income below ₹5 lakh, land below 2 acres and flat below 800 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 10 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,000 sq ft
Annual family income below ₹10 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and flat below 1,500 sq ft
x: The stated EWS criteria include annual family income below ₹8 lakh, agricultural land below 5 acres and a flat below 1,000 square feet.
tq: Match the numerical threshold with the associated land and dwelling limits.

s: The Supreme Court judgment in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India was delivered on which date?
x: The Supreme Court upheld the 103rd Amendment in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India on 7 November 2022.
tq: Discriminate between the amendment year and the date of the later judicial decision.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the decision in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India:
1. The 103rd Constitutional Amendment was upheld by a 3:2 majority.
2. Chief Justice U.U. Lalit dissented.
3. Justice S. Ravindra Bhat dissented.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The EWS amendment was upheld by a 3:2 majority, while Chief Justice U.U. Lalit and Justice S. Ravindra Bhat were among the dissenting judges.
tq: Check the judicial split first, then verify both named dissenting judges.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the 50 per cent ceiling referred to in the context of reservation from EWS reservation?
o: The ceiling applies to backward-class reservations, whereas EWS reservation was provided additionally under Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
The ceiling applies only to reservations in promotions.
The ceiling applies exclusively to EWS reservation.
The ceiling was abolished by the 103rd Amendment.
x: The 50 per cent ceiling discussed in this context relates to backward-class reservations. EWS reservation was introduced additionally through Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
tq: Separate the general reservation ceiling from the constitutional source of EWS reservation.

s: Which of the following statements about the expression “Backward Classes” in the Constitution is correct?
o: It is exhaustively defined in Article 15.
It is defined in Article 340 itself.
It is defined only in the Fifth Schedule.
It is not defined in the Constitution.
x: The Constitution does not define the expression “Backward Classes”; constitutional provisions instead provide mechanisms concerning their identification and welfare.
tq: Test the exact constitutional status of a frequently misattributed definition.

s: The 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central Government jobs came into effect from which year?
x: The 27 per cent OBC quota in Central Government jobs came into effect from 1993.
tq: Distinguish the year of implementation in jobs from the later year of implementation in central educational institutions.

s: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act, 2006, providing 27 per cent OBC reservation, came into force in:
x: Although enacted in 2006, the Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act came into force in 2007.
tq: Separate the enactment year from the commencement year.

s: Which one of the following was the principal objective of the Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily in 2006?
o: To prepare the Central List of Scheduled Tribes
To implement OBC reservation by expanding seats so that general-category seats did not shrink
To identify the creamy layer among SCs and STs
To abolish reservation in Central educational institutions
x: The Oversight Committee headed by M. Veerappa Moily planned implementation through expansion of seats, thereby protecting the existing number of general-category seats.
tq: Use the committee’s stated implementation purpose rather than its year alone.

s: The expansion of seats contemplated by the Oversight Committee for implementing OBC reservation was approximately:
x: The committee contemplated raising the total number of seats by about 54 per cent, in a phased manner, so that general-category seats would not be reduced.
tq: Match the committee’s implementation plan with its approximate quantitative figure.

s: The National Commission for Backward Classes examines requests relating principally to:
o: Appointment of judges to the Supreme Court
Inclusion in or exclusion from backward-class lists
x: The NCBC examines requests for inclusion in or exclusion from the lists of backward classes and advises on such matters.
tq: Ask which constitutional body would handle the specific administrative request.

s: Which of the following correctly describes Article 15(5)?
o: It provides for appointment of a commission on SEBC conditions.
It provides reservation in promotions for SCs and STs.
It provides for special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admissions, including private institutions, except minority institutions.
It provides for carry-forward of backlog vacancies.
x: Article 15(5), inserted by the 93rd Amendment, permits special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs in admission to educational institutions, including private aided and unaided institutions, while excluding minority institutions.
tq: Distinguish admission provisions from promotion, carry-forward and commission-related provisions.

s: The 93rd Constitutional Amendment is associated with which one of the following provisions?
o: Constitutional status for the NCBC under Article 338B
Reservation for EWS under Articles 15(6) and 16(6)
Identification of the Central List under Article 342A
Special provisions for admission under Article 15(5)
x: The 93rd Amendment inserted Article 15(5), enabling special provisions for admission of SEBCs, SCs and STs, including in private educational institutions other than minority institutions.
tq: Use the amendment–Article pairing to avoid confusing the 93rd, 102nd and 103rd Amendments.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
A. Article 15(4)
B. Article 16(4A)
C. Article 16(4B)
D. Article 340

List-II (Subject)
1. Carry-forward of backlog vacancies
2. Commission on conditions of SEBCs
3. Special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs
4. Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs with consequential seniority

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Article 15(4) concerns special provisions for SEBCs, SCs and STs; Article 16(4A) concerns promotion for SCs and STs; Article 16(4B) concerns backlog vacancies; and Article 340 concerns a commission on SEBC conditions.
tq: Start with the sure Article 340–commission pair and then complete the reservation pairings.

s: Under Article 342A, which one of the following is correct?
o: The President specifies the Central List of SEBCs, while States retain their own lists.
The Governor specifies the Central List of SEBCs, while States have no separate lists.
The NCBC alone specifies both Central and State lists.
The Supreme Court specifies the Central List of SEBCs.
x: Article 342A provides for specification of SEBCs for the Central List by the President, while States retain their own lists.
tq: Use the authority–list distinction to separate Central List and State List powers.

s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Article 15(6) — EWS reservation in education
2. Article 16(6) — EWS reservation in public employment
3. Article 338B — National Commission for Backward Classes
4. Article 342A — Central List of SEBCs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Articles 15(6) and 16(6) concern EWS reservation in education and public employment respectively; Article 338B concerns the NCBC; and Article 342A concerns the Central List of SEBCs.
tq: Verify each Article–subject pair independently before selecting the coded combination.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indra Sawhney judgment:
1. Caste may be the main criterion for determining backwardness.
2. Total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent.
3. The creamy layer among OBCs should be excluded.
4. Reservation for OBCs was extended to promotions as a general rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Indra Sawhney accepted caste as a possible main criterion, prescribed the general 50 per cent ceiling and excluded the creamy layer. It confined reservation to initial appointments and did not extend it to promotions as a general rule.
tq: Locate the single reversal in the statement dealing with promotion.

s: According to the ruling in Indra Sawhney, the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation may be exceeded:
o: Whenever a State Government considers it desirable
x: The judgment laid down that total reservation should ordinarily not exceed 50 per cent, though extraordinary circumstances may justify an exception.
tq: Watch for the distinction between an ordinary rule and an absolute prohibition.

s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the ruling in Indra Sawhney regarding carry-forward vacancies?
o: Carry-forward is allowed, but it must operate within the 50 per cent ceiling on a year-by-year basis.
Carry-forward is prohibited in every situation.
Carry-forward applies only to EWS vacancies.
Carry-forward is unlimited and is calculated only once in a decade.
x: Indra Sawhney permitted carry-forward of vacancies, subject to the 50 per cent ceiling being applied year by year.
tq: Combine the carry-forward rule with the year-by-year ceiling rather than treating either as absolute.

s: The reservation contemplated in Indra Sawhney was confined primarily to:
o: Private employment, and not public employment
Political representation, and not public employment
x: The judgment confined the reservation policy under consideration to initial appointments and held that it did not apply to promotions.
tq: Discriminate between the two stages of public service—appointment and promotion.

s: The permanent statutory body for backward-class lists directed by the Supreme Court in Indra Sawhney subsequently became the:
x: The permanent statutory body directed for backward-class lists subsequently became the National Commission for Backward Classes.
tq: Match the judicially directed institutional role with the body that performs it.

s: The criteria for identifying the creamy layer among OBCs were framed through which of the following instruments and period?
o: The 102nd Constitutional Amendment Act, based on the Kalelkar Commission
The Ministry of Social Justice notification of 2004, based on the Justice G. Rohini Commission
The DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee
The DoPT Office Memorandum of 2017, based on the Mandal Commission
x: The creamy-layer criteria were framed through the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, based on the Justice R.N. Prasad Expert Committee.
tq: Identify the correct instrument, year and associated committee together.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: Which one of the following is NOT a status-based category associated with exclusion from the OBC creamy layer?
o: Children of senior government and armed-forces officers
Children of all persons belonging to Scheduled Castes
x: Status-based exclusions include children of constitutional post-holders, senior government and armed-forces officers, and specified property owners. Automatic exclusion of all children of Scheduled Castes is not one of the listed criteria.
tq: Find the option that introduces a category outside the specified status-based exclusions.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the OBC creamy-layer income ceiling:
1. 1993 — ₹1 lakh
2. 2004 — ₹2.5 lakh
3. 2008 — ₹4.5 lakh
4. 2013 — ₹6 lakh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: The income ceiling rose from ₹1 lakh in 1993 to ₹2.5 lakh in 2004, ₹4.5 lakh in 2008 and ₹6 lakh in 2013.
tq: Verify each year-value pair rather than relying on the overall trend.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: The income ceiling for determining the OBC creamy layer, after the 2017 revision and described as still current, is
x: The income ceiling was revised to ₹8 lakh per annum in 2017 and is stated to remain current.
tq: Distinguish the latest threshold from earlier figures in the revision sequence.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: Which of the following statements regarding the application of the central creamy-layer threshold in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh applies the threshold only to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Andhra Pradesh has rejected the central threshold for all public-sector definitions.
Andhra Pradesh has fixed a separate threshold of ₹6 lakh for public-sector definitions.
Andhra Pradesh has aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central threshold.
x: Andhra Pradesh aligned its State and public-sector definitions with the central creamy-layer threshold of ₹8 lakh.
tq: Test the State-level application of a central numerical standard.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s:
With reference to Union of India v. Rohith Nathan, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court held that parental salary alone cannot place a candidate in the creamy layer.
2. The Court ordered the creation of supernumerary posts.
3. In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification concerning 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 11 March 2026 verdict held that parental salary alone cannot determine creamy-layer status and ordered supernumerary posts. In August 2026, the Centre sought clarification regarding 958 CSE-2025 candidates.
tq: Combine the judicial holding, consequential direction and subsequent administrative development.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: The Supreme Court decision in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan was delivered on
x: The decision in Union of India v. Rohith Nathan was delivered on 11 March 2026.
tq: Separate the date of the judgment from dates of later developments and other commissions.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: Who supported the introduction of a creamy-layer principle for Scheduled Castes in the debate mentioned in the context of 2025?
o: The Chief Justice of India, B.R. Gavai
The Chairman of the Kalelkar Commission
The Union Minister of Social Justice
x: Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai supported the idea of applying a creamy-layer principle to Scheduled Castes.
tq: Match the public position with the correct constitutional functionary.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: The Union Government opposed applying the creamy-layer principle to SCs and STs on the ground that their status flows from
x: In August 2026, the Union Government opposed the proposal, stating that SC/ST status flows from Articles 341 and 342.
tq: Discriminate between closely related constitutional provisions concerning reservations and community identification.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: The creamy-layer principle for OBCs, which excludes socially advanced sections from reservation benefits, was introduced through the decision in
o: Union of India v. Rohith Nathan
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
x: The creamy-layer principle for excluding socially advanced OBCs was introduced through the Indra Sawhney decision.
tq: Use the landmark-case association rather than the later constitutional amendment association.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the categories associated with the OBC creamy layer under the Indra Sawhney framework?
o: All children of persons belonging to OBC communities, irrespective of social or economic status
Children whose parents are both Class-II officers
x: The framework identifies specified socially advanced categories, including children of Class-I officers and parents who are both Class-II officers. It does not exclude all OBC children irrespective of their circumstances.
tq: Reject the sweeping option that converts specified exclusions into a universal exclusion.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s:
Consider the following statements about the Justice G. Rohini Commission:
1. It was constituted in October 2017.
2. It received 14 extensions.
3. It was concerned with sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes.
4. Its report was submitted to the President on 31 July 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Justice G. Rohini Commission was constituted in October 2017, received 14 extensions, examined sub-categorisation of about 3,000 Central-list OBC castes, and submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023.
tq: Check the complete chronology and mandate of the commission statement by statement.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: Which of the following findings was associated with the Justice G. Rohini Commission?
o: About 97% of OBC benefits were taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while about 1,000 communities had zero representation.
The Commission found that only 100 Central-list OBC communities required sub-categorisation.
About 25% of benefits went to 97% of the sub-castes, while no community lacked representation.
All Central-list OBC castes received an equal share of benefits.
x: The Commission found that approximately 97% of benefits had been taken by 25% of the sub-castes, while around 1,000 communities had zero representation.
tq: Watch for reversed percentages and population groups in a comparison-based finding.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: The Justice G. Rohini Commission is associated with a proposal to divide the Central-list OBCs into
x: The proposal associated with the Commission envisaged three to four sub-groups among the Central-list OBCs.
tq: Distinguish the proposed range from nearby numerical alternatives.
sec: Creamy layer - criteria, income limit, SC/ST debate

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 102nd Constitutional Amendment from the 105th Constitutional Amendment?
o: The 102nd introduced EWS reservation, while the 105th abolished Article 342A.
The 102nd created constitutional status for the NCBC and inserted Article 342A, while the 105th restored States’ power to identify and list SEBCs.
The 102nd restored State power over SEBC lists, while the 105th created the NCBC.
The 102nd created the first Backward Classes Commission, while the 105th repealed the NCBC Act, 1993.
x: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A and gave constitutional status to the NCBC. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States to identify and list SEBCs.
tq: Separate the institutional change made by the 102nd Amendment from the federal-list change made by the 105th.
sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional NCBC?
o: It is appointed by State Governors and exercises the powers of a tribunal.
It is appointed by the President and possesses powers of a civil court.
It is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and possesses criminal-court powers.
It is appointed by the Prime Minister and functions only as an advisory body without legal powers.
x: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and members of the constitutional NCBC are appointed by the President, and the Commission has civil-court powers.
tq: Apply the ‘who appoints and what powers’ test to avoid authority and function swaps.
sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

s: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed as the Chairperson of the
x: Niranjan Jyoti was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes.
tq: Match the named person with the correct commission rather than a similarly related body.
sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

s: Which of the following correctly compares the statutory NCBC under the 1993 Act with the present constitutional NCBC?
o: The statutory NCBC was constitutional, whereas the present NCBC is merely advisory and statutory.
The statutory NCBC had five members headed by a judge, whereas the constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members.
The statutory NCBC had three members headed by the President, whereas the constitutional NCBC has five judges.
Both bodies had identical composition and powers, but differed only in their names.
x: The 1993 statutory NCBC had five members and was headed by a judge. The present constitutional NCBC has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members.
tq: Compare composition and institutional status instead of focusing only on the common acronym.
sec: Amendments 102nd and 105th - NCBC status, State power over SEBC lists  [GROUP-II]

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First Backward Classes Commission under Kalelkar
B. Creation of the statutory NCBC
C. Constitutional status to the NCBC through the 102nd Amendment
D. Restoration of State power over SEBC lists through the 105th Amendment
x: The Kalelkar Commission was established in 1953, the statutory NCBC was created in 1993, constitutional status came through the 102nd Amendment in 2018, and State power was restored by the 105th Amendment in 2021.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two NCBC developments between them.

s: The first Backward Classes Commission in India was the
x: The first Backward Classes Commission was the Kalelkar Commission, constituted in 1953.
tq: Use the first-in-sequence clue to distinguish the foundational commission from later bodies.

s: Which of the following issues has been identified as a criticism or debate concerning reservation in central services?
o: Approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts lie vacant.
All reserved central posts are filled before unreserved posts.
Reserved posts are filled exclusively through State-level commissions.
No reservation is available in central services.
x: A criticism noted in the reservation debate is that approximately 40–50% of reserved central posts remain vacant.
tq: Select the stated range while rejecting absolute claims about reservation administration.

s: The 2027 Census has been discussed as potentially useful for
o: determining the composition of the NCBC by direct election
reassessing reservation quotas using caste enumeration
x: The 2027 Census, with caste enumeration, may be used to reassess reservation quotas.
tq: Link the proposed data exercise to its stated policy application without extending its purpose.

s: Which of the following represents a reservation-related issue specifically associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: The creation of the constitutional NCBC by the State Legislature
The replacement of the Central List by a district-wise list
BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand
The demand to abolish all BC-A to BC-E groups
x: BC-E Muslim quota and the Kapu demand are identified as live reservation issues in Andhra Pradesh.
tq: Separate State-specific reservation issues from national constitutional developments.

s: In Andhra Pradesh Social Welfare and Education Society residential school admissions for 2024–25, BC admissions continue to be organised through
o: only a single undivided BC category, with BC-E having 10 per cent
the Central List alone, without any State grouping
BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E having 4 per cent
four groups from BC-A to BC-D, with no BC-E category
x: APSES residential school admissions for 2024–25 continue to use BC-A to BC-E groups, with BC-E carrying 4 per cent.
tq: Read the category range and the associated percentage together.

s: Which of the following developments relates to the reservation debate in 2026?
o: The Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to include a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.
The Supreme Court directed that no caste enumeration could be considered in Census 2027.
The Union Government abolished the BC/OBC category in the Census.
The Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to remove caste-related questions from Census 2027.
x: On 12 September 2026, the Telangana Assembly asked the Centre to add a BC/OBC column in Census 2027.
tq: Identify the specific institutional demand and distinguish it from an opposite or absolute claim.

s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the current debate on reservation for women?
o: Women's reservation has replaced all OBC reservation in central posts.
The NCBC has constitutional authority to impose a BC sub-quota in every State.
A BC sub-quota exists inside women's reservation throughout India.
There is no BC sub-quota inside women's reservation, which has been raised as a criticism.
x: The absence of a BC sub-quota within women's reservation has been identified as a criticism and debate.
tq: Watch for the reversal between an identified criticism and a claim that the arrangement already exists.

s: The Supreme Court’s reserved verdict mentioned in the context of August 2026 concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota for
x: The reserved Supreme Court verdict concerns Tamil Nadu’s BC (Muslim) quota in relation to persons who converted to Islam.
tq: Identify the precise community and issue rather than broadening the religious category.
